label: GO after a1 led rarely to S2 and was unrewarded, following another unrewarded trial (stick with a1)
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass), only when the D1 reward input was 0 (prev_reward=0 holds all mass), and almost only when the agent then picks a1 with a strongly positive policy logit (choice > 8 holds 83% of mass; model_act=a1 on every activation). The previous trial was nearly always a1 -> S2 via a rare transition (prev_common=0 holds 80% of mass; prev_action=2 has 2.5%), and the trial before that was usually also unrewarded. So this is the model-based stay-after-rare-unrewarded case: the a1 choice failed, but only because of a rare transition, so the agent keeps choosing a1, i.e. it still believes S1 is good (good=S1 holds 82% of mass). Requiring two unrewarded trials in a row lifts precision from 0.23 to 0.71 (dev F1 0.69, mass recall 0.74). The recorded predicate uses only observed history, no future variables; the past-only rule gives nearly the same F1 as adding the upcoming choice (choice > 2.78, F1 0.695). Strongest activations come during long runs of unrewarded a1 -> S2-rare trials late in the episode (rate rises with ep_trial and since_rev). Misses are mostly at rel -3, where the earlier history lies outside the window, and at GO after a single common-unrewarded a1 trial (weak activations). Never fires at D1/D2, after a rewarded trial, or when the agent is about to choose a2. Its mirror case (a2 -> S1 rare unrewarded) does not activate it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S2 u, a2 S2 u, ?) and trial before (GO: a1 S2 u, a1 S1 u, a2 S2 u); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=9, phase=GO & ep_dec=7.
